title: Soft Steamed Rice and Lentil Idli with Coconut Chutney
summary: Rice and urad dal are soaked, ground and fermented overnight into a bubbly batter, then steamed in moulds and served with a fresh coconut, chilli and ginger chutney.
equipment: large bowl (at least 3 litres) and a clean tea towel
idli stand with moulds (or a 20 cm heatproof plate)
large lidded pot that holds the stand
butter knife or spoon dipped in water

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Rinse the rice and poha together until the water runs clear and cover them with plenty of water in one bowl. Rinse the urad dal with the fenugreek and cover with water in the other bowl. Soak both for 4-12 hours.

steps.title: Grind
steps.text: Drain the dal and blend it with about 120 ml cold water, adding more a spoonful at a time, for 3-5 minutes until very smooth, light and fluffy; scrape it into the large bowl. Drain the rice and poha and blend with about 240 ml cold water until fine, like semolina, then stir into the dal with the salt. The batter should drop thickly from a spoon. Grinding separately makes the dal airier, which gives softer idli.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Cover with the towel and leave somewhere warm (25-30 °C, such as an oven with only the light on) for 8-12 hours, until about doubled, bubbly and pleasantly sour. Stir gently just to combine; don't beat out the air.

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Bring 3 cm water to the boil in the pot. Oil the moulds and fill each three-quarters full. Set the stand in the pot, cover and steam over medium-high heat for 12-15 minutes, until a knife pushed into an idli comes out clean. Rest off the heat for 2 minutes, then loosen with the wet knife and unmould. Repeat with the remaining batter.

steps.title: Make the chutney
steps.text: Soak the coconut in the warm water for 10 minutes, then blend it with the chilli, ginger, lemon juice and 1/4 tsp salt to a thick, slightly textured paste. Heat the oil in the small pan, add the mustard seeds and, when they pop, the curry leaves, then pour over the chutney.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve 6 hot idli per person with the coconut chutney, and with sambar if you have it.

tips: Warmth is everything; in a cool kitchen the batter can take up to 18 hours to rise.
Don't overfill the moulds; the batter puffs as it steams.
Leftover batter keeps in the fridge for 2 days and makes good dosa-style pancakes.
Idli rice or parboiled rice gives the softest texture; basmati makes them crumbly.
storage: Refrigerate idli and chutney separately within 1 hour and use within 3 days. Re-steam idli for 5 minutes, or reheat once until piping hot (74 °C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
